transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Time: 16:30 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (RDSE) — Alex Kim, Priya Rao, Diego Morales, Sara Li (OceanSky)

Summary (auto): quick demo of embeddings + reranking endpoints, walked through embedding generation, index + retrieval, then the reranker endpoint for final scoring. Discussed security and pilot next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. With me is Jordan our SE, and Samir who helps with pilot onboarding. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Alex (OceanSky): Good thanks, Alex here. Excited to see how this could replace some of our current search stack.
[00:11] Priya: Hi all — Priya, engineering lead on search. We've got a FAISS-based pipeline today and curious about improvements in relevance and latency.
[00:20] Jordan (Redwood): Awesome, we'll start with a quick architecture overview then jump into a live playground — embeddings endpoint, vector store integration, retrieval, and the rerank endpoint which re-scores candidate docs with context.
[00:32] Diego: Quick Q before you dive in — does Redwood host the vector index or we keep it on prem?
[00:37] Samir (Redwood): Good question. For hosted mode we typically leave the vector index customer-managed but many customers use hosted storage + our endpoints for embeddings and reranker. We also integrate easily with Pinecone, Milvus, or you can keep FAISS on your infra.
[00:49] Alex: So you'd run embeddings as a hosted API call and then we push embeddings to our FAISS cluster?
[00:55] Jordan: Exactly. Embedding generation via the hosted /embeddings endpoint — low-latency batch or streaming — then flush into your vector store. For rerank we provide a reranker endpoint where you send candidate doc ids + context and we return refreshed scores and optional explanation tokens.
[01:10] Priya: What about latency — our p95 for search is around 120ms and we have a tight SLO.
[01:16] Jordan: On hosted, typical rerank call with a compact model is around 40-120ms depending on sequence length and batch; we can tune by using a smaller reranker or quantized variant. There's some tradeoff: smaller models lower cost/latency but might reduce subtle relevance lifts.
[01:31] Alex: Do you have numbers vs our FAISS + in-house reranker?
[01:35] Maya: We ran benchmarks with customers where embeddings generation was comparable and reranker often improved NDCG by 3-8% at top 10. Jordan, do you have the sheet?
[01:44] Jordan: Yep — I've got a benchmark template I'll share. Example: 1k queries, retrieval candidates 50, reranker added about 0.05s per query but improved MRR. We also show cost per 10k queries in that sheet.
[01:56] Diego: You mentioned quantized variants — hosted supports that?
[02:00] Jordan: Yes, hosted models include quantization profiles (8-bit, 4-bit) under the hood in our runtime. For aggressive latency targets we recommend our quantized reranker profile + caching of prefixes when possible. Note sometimes the transcriber calls KV cache "K-V cache" or "K V cache" — it's the same concept.
[02:18] Priya: On security — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML/Okta), and customer-managed KMS for keys. Any dealbreakers?
[02:26] Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II, we support SAML/Okta SSO, and for Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM. For hosted we have KMS integrations and audit logs that meet most enterprise requirements. I'll drop the security pack in the follow-up.
[02:40] Sara (Legal): Do you retain embeddings or request contents on hosted? Need clarity for data retention and PII concerns.
[02:46] Samir: Hosted mode by default does not persist request-level content beyond short-term logs for troubleshooting; we have options for strict retention and redaction, and Private deployments give you full control. We'll send the data flow diagram.
[02:59] Alex: Walk me through a typical search flow again end-to-end.
[03:03] Jordan: Sure — step 1: user query => normalize => call /embeddings to get vector; step 2: nearest neighbor search in your vector store (FAISS/Pinecone/Milvus) to get top-K candidates; step 3: call Redwood rerank endpoint with query + top-K doc text/metadata, reranker returns scores and optionally tokens/explanations; step 4: apply business logic (boosts, freshness) and return results.
[03:28] Alex: Regarding cost, do you charge per embedding call and per rerank call?
[03:33] Maya: Yes, hosted pricing is per embedding unit and per rerank request. We'll send a clear pricing example for your query volumes in the deck.
[03:40] Priya: For our traffic spike patterns — we see bursty search during content drops — how do you handle autoscaling?
[03:47] Samir: Hosted autoscaling is automatic; we provide burst capacity and also recommend a small local cache for top queries. For Dedicated you can reserve GPUs for predictable throughput.
[03:58] Diego: Can the reranker do function/tool like structured output? We sometimes need highlight spans for UI.
[04:04] Jordan: Reranker can return token-level highlights and structured metadata (we support structured output formats). The highlight quality depends on prompt and model choice.
[04:14] Alex: Let's see the live demo.
[04:16] Jordan: Switching screens — this is the Redwood Console. Here is the embeddings playground: you POST to /v1/embeddings with text, get back a vector. I'll paste an example curl.
[04:30] Jordan: [shows curl] curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"how to reset password"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' — response is a vector (768 dims in this example).
[04:45] Priya: Do you surface vector dims and model version?
[04:48] Jordan: Yes model_version is returned and you can pin model versions in config.
[04:52] Alex: How do you recommend we store vectors — we currently use on-prem FAISS, considering a move to Pinecone.
[04:58] Samir: If you keep FAISS, you can push embeddings directly; Pinecone or Milvus are simpler managed options. For pilot we can integrate with your FAISS snapshot — Jordan will share sample ETL.
[05:12] Jordan: Now the reranker demo — I'll send a request with query + 10 candidate snippets. The reranker returns re-ordering and scores.
[05:19] Jordan: [remote request] sending payload... response in 85ms — reordered top 3 and provided confidence scores.
[05:26] Diego: I noticed the model trimmed some HTML badly in snippets — is cleaning recommended?
[05:30] Jordan: Yes pre-processing is important. We recommend a light HTML strip + preserve key metadata fields. Also for long docs we pass excerpts for rerank.
[05:40] Alex: Are there limits on context length?
[05:43] Jordan: Reranker can handle fairly long contexts but cost and latency increase with length; we often do retrieval-augmented rerank where we only pass passages.
[05:50] Priya: Any pitfalls migrating from our FAISS scoring pipeline?
[05:52] Jordan: Common ones: mismatch in tokenization, different embedding dimensionality, and freshness of embeddings. We usually suggest a smoke test of 1k queries and compare MRR/CTR.
[06:05] Maya: I'll highlight the pilot: 4-week pilot, we run benchmarks vs your FAISS, Redwood provides test harness and a pair of models (compact + standard reranker) and we collaborate on evaluation.
[06:15] Alex: That sounds good. What's the expected work we need to do?
[06:19] Maya: Provide sample corpus and queries, share access or snapshots, one engineer for integration. Jordan: we'll set up a runner and show dashboards — Console has per-route latency/cost.
[06:30] Priya: Do you expose token-level cost breakdown?
[06:33] Jordan: Yes Console shows token cost, latency, per-route breakdowns and can emit tracing hooks.
[06:40] Sara: For legal — we need a DPA and details on retention.
[06:44] Maya: We'll attach the DPA and security pack.
[06:47] Alex: Any specific SDKs — we use Python and Node.
[06:50] Jordan: Official SDKs for Python/Node, plus examples for pushing embeddings to FAISS.
[06:56] Diego: For the reranker model, can we use a custom fine-tuned reranker?
[06:59] Jordan: We support custom rerankers via model onboarding — Private or Dedicated is often chosen for fully custom weights but we also support limited fine-tuning and prompts in hosted. We'll clarify the options in the doc.
[07:12] Priya: Are there any compliance options if we need data residency in EU?
[07:16] Samir: We have EU cloud regions and Private deployments for strict residency.
[07:20] Alex: Let's talk benchmarks — can you share the benchmark template now?
[07:23] Jordan: Yep sharing in chat — it's a Google sheet with columns: query, ground_truth_id, retrieved_topk, reranked_order, latency_ms, cost_usd. We'll populate example rows.
[07:35] Maya: Small aside — some customers compare us to OpenAI rerank and Pinecone as a combined solution. Anything on that?
[07:41] Jordan: The main diff is we provide an integrated rerank + embeddings product with production-grade runtime and observability; some teams stitch OpenAI + Pinecone but they lose rollout controls and cost transparency.
[07:53] Diego: Any preview of expected cost for 10M queries/month?
[07:56] Maya: We'll provide a modelled cost — it depends on candidate K and model choices; that's in the pricing deck.
[08:03] Alex: One more technical — how deterministic are rerank scores? We need reproducible A/B tests.
[08:08] Jordan: Determinism depends on model variant — we can pin seeds and model_version for repeatability; for exact determinism we recommend pinned model + config.
[08:18] Priya: Ok let's recap next steps.
[08:21] Maya: Recap — Maya sends pricing + security docs, Jordan sends benchmark template + ETL examples, OceanSky to send sample artifacts, schedule pilot kickoff.
[08:30] Alex: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:33] Maya: Thank you — ping us in slack or email. We'll follow up with dates.
[08:38] End of recording.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional ASR errors ("K V cache" vs "KV cache"), minor name transcriptions. Some overlap/crosstalk omitted.
